item.title: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>DoorDash reduced grocery reorder latency from 16 to 2 seconds by precomputing recurring purchase needs using batch LLM inference and deterministic validation. Live catalog resolution keeps product selections current, while an editable shopping interface avoids unnecessary model calls. The company reports that shopping list views doubled and the flow’s order rate increased by approximately 34%</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Netflix Treats GPU Reliability as a Distributed Systems Problem
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-gpu-distributed-systems/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576903003.jpg"/><p>Netflix has detailed how it is building a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference, using layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep jobs running despite hardware failures.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: Presentation: The Ladder Is Missing Rungs: Engineering Progression When AI Ate the Middle
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/ai-software-engineering-pipeline/en/mediumimage/alasdair-allan-medium-1791451156021.jpeg"/><p>Alasdair Allan discusses empirical research from METR and Anthropic on AI coding adoption. He explains the "supervision paradox," where reliance on AI tools disrupts junior skill development, risks institutional context loss, and threatens the long-term engineering pipeline needed to oversee autonomous systems effectively.</p> <i>By Alasdair Allan</i>

item.title: Netflix Titus Adds Single-Tenant VM Isolation for Containers
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/netflix-titus-kubernetes-microvm/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793268697529.jpg"/><p>Netflix has added single-tenant Titus, a mode that runs one task alone on its own right-sized EC2 instance. The Compute/Platform team still owns and patches the host, so application teams keep the same API and deployment path</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>

item.title: Article: InfoQ AI, ML and Data Engineering Trends Report - 2026
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/ai-ml-data-engineering-trends-2026/en/headerimage/ai-ml-de-graph-2026-1793191771570.jpg"/><p>This InfoQ Trends Report offers readers a comprehensive overview of emerging trends and technologies in the areas of AI, ML, and Data Engineering. This report summarizes the InfoQ editorial team’s and external guests' view on the current trends in AI and ML technologies and what to look out for in the next 12 months.</p> <i>By Srini Penchikala, Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals</i>

item.title: Podcast: AI, ML, and Data Engineering InfoQ Trends Report 2026
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/ai-ml-data-engineering-trends-2026/en/smallimage/trend-reports-thumbnail-1793181579584.jpg"/><p>In this episode, members of the InfoQ AI and ML editorial staff and friends of InfoQ discuss the current trends in the domain of AI, ML and Data Engineering. One of the regular features of InfoQ are the trends reports, which each focus on a different aspect of software dev. These reports provide the InfoQ readers and listeners with a high-level overview of the topics to pay attention to this year.</p> <i>By Chip Huyen, Daniel Dominguez, Hien Luu, Arthur Casals</i>

item.title: Microsoft Retires Azure Deployment Environments with No Replacement Product
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ade-dev-box-retirement/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792499241111.jpg"/><p>Azure Deployment Environments retires on February 22, 2027 and Microsoft names no successor, telling teams to use Bicep or ARM templates directly. Microsoft Dev Box follows on September 18, 2028, pointed at Windows 365, which Microsoft says is not a one-to-one replacement. Remaining Dev Box workloads should expect deletion.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Google Adopts DPoP to Strengthen OAuth 2.0 Against Token Theft and Replay Attacks
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Google's OAuth Platform has recently introduces support for Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP), an OAuth 2.0 security mechanism designed to mitigate token theft and replay attacks.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Bug0 Releases QA Agent to Automate Regression Testing With Cached Playwright Replays
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/bug0-agent-testing-cached-replay/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793286673185.jpg"/><p>QA Agent is a new source-available Playwright library for agentic browser regression testing. The agent associates test instructions expressed in natural language to actions on the user interface, caches those when appropriate for faster CI replays, remapping them to test specifications when the user interface changes. Verification is based on multi-model consensus and vision model evaluations.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

item.title: How to Make Artificial Intelligence More Environmentally Sustainable
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/AI-environmentally-sustainable/en/headerimage/header-1793174464846.jpg"/><p>IT is responsible for about 2 - 4% of all global emissions, and electricity use at Microsoft and Google has climbed because of AI, according to their own reports. Sustainability ought to be a top-level architectural concern. Some recommendations are: use pre-built and smaller models, run compute where low-carbon electricity is abundant, and train on renewable energy.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

item.title: QCon AI New York 2026 Program Committee Picks: Agent Identity, Context Costs, and Open-Source Infere
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-pc-picks/en/headerimage/qcon-ai-newyork-2026-pc-picks-1793192613417.jpg"/><p>Who authorizes an agent’s actions, and how should teams manage growing context costs? The QCon AI New York 2026 program committee shares six session picks that tackle these questions, alongside open-source inference, agent standards, and audio AI.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

item.title: Anthropic Says Nobody Needs a Mental Model of Claude Code. Practitioners Are Testing That
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/anthropic-code-review/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792959100117.jpg"/><p>Anthropic has published how the Claude Code team reviews code now that Claude writes roughly 90% of it, including a claim that nobody keeps a complete mental model of the codebase. The post documents a pull request that ran more than fifty review rounds overnight, a reviewer spending most of its effort on pre-existing code, and a control the team says it does not yet have.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Datadog Builds a Specialist AI Model for SRE Investigations
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/datadog-scout-sre-model/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793038066919.jpg"/><p>Datadog has released Scout, a model trained to investigate production problems. It runs inside Bits Investigation, the company's AI SRE product, where it can pick up an alert, look through telemetry and suggest what caused the problem. Datadog engineers and a small number of customers are using it in a closed preview.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-web-search-api/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1791616850849.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has recently launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway. Available through REST APIs and Cloudflare Workers, it provides unified logging, access controls, and billing, and supports bring-your-own-provider keys.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

item.title: Airbnb Cuts Recommendation Staleness from 2 Days to Seconds with Chronon
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Airbnb extended its Chronon feature platform with Push Mode and Near Real-Time Model Transform to update sequence-based recommendation embeddings within seconds. The architecture reduced embedding staleness from nearly two days to under a minute and improved offline NDCG by 1.67%, while online testing increased uncancelled bookings by approximately one-third of a percent.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Presentation: Wrangling Telemetry at Scale: A Guide to Self-Hosted Observability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/self-hosted-observability-stack-tradeoffs/en/mediumimage/colin-douch-medium-1791450600829.jpeg"/><p>Colin Douch shares battle-tested strategies for building and scaling self-hosted observability stacks. He explains how to effectively correlate metrics, structured logs, and distributed traces using open-source tooling like Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, and Jaeger, while navigating the engineering trade-offs of avoiding SaaS vendor lock-in.</p> <i>By Colin Douch</i>

item.title: Microsoft's October Security Update Fixes 1,400+ Vulnerabilities, One Exploited in the Wild
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/microsoft-october-2026-patch/en/headerimage/microsoft-october-patch-1793129871505.jpeg"/><p>Microsoft's latest monthly security update addresses 1415 vulnerabilities across multiple products. One vulnerability affecting Windows Shell has been exploited in the wild, while 85 are classified as critical. Affected products include Windows OS, Office, Exchange, .NET, Edge, as well as potentially Hyper-V and Azure components.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

item.title: Chrome Opens Trial for the Email Verification API: Letting Sites Verify Without Sending Emails
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/chrome-email-verification/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793091215457.jpg"/><p>Google has opened a Chrome origin trial for the Email Verification API, a WICG proposal that lets the browser confirm email ownership without sending a message. Gmail is the first provider. Developers add form hints and validate a signed token server-side. Commenters question the privacy benefit, and the API is best used as a progressive enhancement.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Cloudflare Opens Quicksilver to Customers as Workers KV Instant, Inside a 1 MB Envelope
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has put Quicksilver, the internal key-value store behind nearly every request it serves, into private beta as a Workers KV mode. Reads resolve in 1.62 ms at p99 against 287 ms for classic KV. The constraints decide the use case: 10,000 keys, one megabyte per namespace, and one write per namespace per second.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: Uber Moves beyond CPU Cores with Performance-Aware Scheduling for Stateful Workloads
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/uber-cpu-stateful-workloads/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792576315045.jpg"/><p>Uber has introduced Normalized Compute Units (NCUs) to make CPU allocation more consistent across its highly heterogeneous server fleet.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

item.title: AWS Shows Use of AI Agents to Triage Linux Kernel CVEs
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/aws-ai-agents-linux-kernel-cves/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793031817205.jpg"/><p>Engineers from Amazon Web Services (AWS) have described how the team that maintains the Linux kernel for EC2 infrastructure handles kernel CVEs. The process combines an automated filter, an AI agent and human review. The team also argues that it needs to move to newer long-term-support (LTS) kernels, as older branches collect fixes that are never backported.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

item.title: Cloudflare and VoidZero Introduce tsrs: an AI-Generated Rust Port of TypeScript
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-tsrs-ai-typescript/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793039825386.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare, VoidZero and Max Schwenk announced tsrs, an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built with the TypeScript team's involvement. Cloudflare claims up to 8x faster checking and 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, though one test against 7.1 beta showed 2.7x. It lacks watch mode and a language server, and exits with code 2 on type errors.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: Developers Reporting Double-Digit Weekly Time Savings from AI Fell from 68% to 26%
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/atlassian-devex-2026/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793026389174.jpg"/><p>Atlassian’s State of Developer Experience 2026 finds the share of developers saving ten or more hours a week with AI dropped from 68% to 26% year over year, while only 28% report noticeably less friction than before AI. Engineering leaders report spending more time managing and correcting AI output than developers do.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: AGNTCon + MCPCon 2026: Agentic AI Foundation Adds Four Projects as MCP Turns to Security
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/agntcon-mcpcon-2026/en/headerimage/agntcon-header-1792936265463.jpg"/><p>At AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026, the Agentic AI Foundation added OpenSandbox, Open Responses, Agent Skills, and OpenEnv, reaching ten projects in its first year. Keynotes from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and UC Berkeley focused on MCP in production, security, and agents with their own identities.</p> <i>By Andrew Hoblitzell</i>

item.title: OpenTofu 1.13 Lets Module Authors Reduce Unknown Values at Plan Time
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/opentofu-1-13-unknown-values/en/headerimage/header-1792823798248.jpeg"/><p>OpenTofu 1.13 adds convert and assume... functions that let module authors give the planner type and value hints for unknown values, so more expressions resolve during tofu plan. If a value unknown during planning later violates a guarantee, OpenTofu reports an error during apply.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

item.title: Readyon Builds Four Layer Tenant Isolation for Multi Tenant Amazon EKS
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>ReadyOn has detailed a four-layer tenant isolation architecture for its Harmony platform on Amazon EKS. The design combines Kubernetes namespaces, dedicated Karpenter node pools, VPC security groups, and per-tenant Aurora databases, with controls evaluated against a 10-stage multi-tenant threat model focused on cross-tenant access and lateral movement.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

item.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-auto-router/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792492628413.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

item.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/ngrx-22-angular/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792664456149.jpg"/><p>NgRx 22 adds experimental resource extensions that change Angular's resource behavior, so value() is retained during reloads and no longer throws on errors. It also introduces dynamic deep signals for union types, a SignalStoreFeatureType utility, and ESLint v10 support. Upgrading requires Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and most breaking changes have automated migrations.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

item.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
item.content:encoded: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/10/nestjs-12-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792168374584.jpg"/><p>NestJS version 12 has been released, transitioning core packages to ESM and adding Standard Schema validation. It updates the CLI and introduces an observability SDK. Key changes include project generation choices between CJS and ESM, improved validation options, and lifecycle project hooks. Users will need Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. Migration guides are available for upgrading.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>
